lens: responsive mobile task completion, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The frozen responsive build retains the passed 375x812, 390x844, 430x932, and 844x390 checks with no horizontal overflow, 44-pixel critical controls, and zero unexpected console errors. The new source-authority and retry fixes pass production-build desktop browser checks. A real virtual keyboard, VoiceOver, background/relaunch, and physical-device browser flow remain untested.
findings.user_impact: Responsive Web is highly usable in emulation, but assistive and device-lifecycle reliability is not yet proven for a paid promise.
findings.recommendation: Run the full production loop on small and large physical phones with VoiceOver, accessibility text, virtual keyboard, landscape, background, relaunch, and an interrupted retry.
findings.verification: Evidence, identity, review, approval, unknown recovery, source authority, history, and deletion remain named, ordered, reachable, unclipped, and duplicate-free across the physical-device matrix.

strengths: The first task, relationship state, and one next action remain legible at 375 and 390 pixels.
The fixed navigation and boundary-case footer do not intercept the final sidebar action.
Conflict history and verified outcome remain readable in landscape without horizontal scrolling.
Every directly checked critical interaction target in the responsive matrix meets the 44-pixel floor.
missing_evidence: Real virtual-keyboard and physical-device background/relaunch evidence.
A complete authenticated production mobile loop.
open_questions: Does the bottom dock remain non-obstructive when a real keyboard and accessibility text are active together?
